source.title: We Inspected Every Head In GPT-2 Small using SAEs So You Don’t Have To
source.authors: robertzk; Connor Kissane; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE feature attribution and qualitative head interpretation to assess a head role, rather than the original circuit and loss measurements.
record.gate_note: The post lists GPT-2 small L10H7 as the copy suppression head when describing its qualitative validation against previously studied heads. It gives no L10H7-specific examples, behavioral measurement, or intervention. Other reported head experiments, including the L10H2 ablations, do not test this claim.
record.test_reason: The post interprets L10H7 from its top-10 attention-SAE features, a method independent of the original's circuit analysis. It reports that this recovers the head's copy-suppression role, as a validation result. That bears weakly on V1 (the head's salient role) and on no other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say their SAE interpretations match previously studied heads, including 10.7 as the copy suppression head. They call the top-10-feature review a rough heuristic that may not fully capture a head's role.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE decoder-weight attribution and manual interpretation of top features, rather than the original study's circuit and behavioral analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that decoder-weight attribution is an imperfect proxy for feature attribution and recommend FVE for reproductions; they do not report an L10H7-specific comparison.
record.problems: For L10H7, the evidence is only a qualitative role label; the post reports no head-specific behavioral test, intervention, or uncertainty. The authors warn that examining only the top 10 features with an imperfect attribution proxy can miss roles or produce misleading impressions.
record.rows_left_out: Unrelated findings about other heads and the L10H2 synthetic-task ablations were left out because they do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether suppression is specific to tokens both predicted upstream and present in context. How much of the head's behaviour is copy suppression. How the role holds across the distribution.
No QK/OV circuit or loss-effect analysis.
No upstream ablation or self-repair measurement.
No negative name mover or cross-model comparison of copy suppression. The limitations note only that some IOI heads lacked representative features.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is very thin: one line in a validation list plus a dashboard link. The post does not say how many of L10H7's top 10 features reflect copy suppression. L10H7 is absent from both the plausibly monosemantic list and the asterisked notable heads. This might imply the top features are mixed, but the text does not state it, so no limits_scope label is given. The annotator only 'mostly' did not know which heads were previously studied, so L10H7's label may not be blind.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report the detailed condition that earlier components predict a token also present in context, nor establish how broadly the role holds across the training distribution.
No L10H7 QK/OV circuit analysis or loss-effect estimate is reported.
Calibration and overconfidence in copying are not measured for L10H7.
No upstream copier ablation or self-repair measurement is reported for L10H7.
The post does not test whether negative heads in narrow tasks or other models and sizes share this role.
The post does not measure the relative contribution of copy suppression and other mechanisms to self-repair.

It says nothing about the 'mainly' or 'across the training distribution' strength of V1.

relation.reason: The authors report their own qualitative head interpretation matching copy suppression, providing weak evidence about the role rather than merely citing it.

tranche.reason: Manual interpretation of SAE features attributed by decoder weights provides a different method bearing on L10H7's role.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is paraphrased accurately. L10H7-specific features and quantitative suppression evidence are not reproduced in the text; the authors warn that inspecting ten salient features can miss other roles.

statements.correction: Authors: Robert Krzyzanowski, Connor Kissane, Arthur Conmy, Neel Nanda. Annotator mostly did not know which heads had previously been studied. Top 10 features ranked by decoder-weight attribution; L10H7 identified as copy suppression; no quantitative copy-suppression result reported.
statements.problem: The qualitative result and method are accurate. Comparison of author groups cannot be verified because the permitted material does not give the original study's author list.

statements.correction: Qualitative recovery of L10H7's copy-suppression role using SAE features; no measurement of its prevalence across the training distribution. Authors: Robert Krzyzanowski, Connor Kissane, Arthur Conmy, Neel Nanda. Original-study author overlap not established by supplied material.
statements.problem: The role-label result and lack of distribution-wide measurement are accurate for this study. Its inclusion among studies sharing no author with the original, and consequently the author-overlap count, cannot be verified from the permitted material.
